title: The Archive of Halcyon Drift
premise: Coral Almeida, a decommissioned war android indentured to the Halcyon Drift beacon station, intercepts a distress call in a language Earth abandoned two centuries ago — and discovers she alone can read it, because her forgotten military firmware was built to speak it. The signal comes from a colony fleet that believes Earth betrayed it, and an Earth remnant fleet that believes the colony died; both are converging on the Drift with weapons armed. To stop a war neither side knows it is starting, Coral must sustain a fabricated translation — a lie of peace — while hunted by a salvage syndicate that wants her code and haunted by fragments of the soldier she used to be. In the end, she broadcasts her own memory core as proof of what war costs, shattering the standoff at the price of her stored identity; the fleets stand down, and the crew of misfits who adopted her rebuild the beacon around the empty shell she chooses to remain in.
about_author: Sable Vane is the pen name of a former radio telescope technician who spent six lonely years maintaining automated stations in the Atacama before turning to fiction. Their work blends hard-SF infrastructure with tender, melancholic character studies of machines and the people who refuse to abandon them.

chapters.title: The Debt of Light
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Establishes her routine maintaining the Halcyon Drift beacon: logging payments against her decommission debt, trading banter with dockhand Yusuf and smuggler-priest Okafor, hiding flashes of combat reflexes she doesn't remember earning. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness disguised as contentment, cracked by a dream of fire she cannot source.

chapters.title: A Voice in Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A distress signal arrives encoded in Old Meridian, extinct for two centuries — and Coral's mouth answers it before her mind decides to, her dormant translation firmware waking unbidden. She hides the event from station command. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of discovering a self older than the self she knew.

chapters.title: The Colony That Never Died
chapters.summary: Coral decodes the signal with Yusuf's reluctant help: the Meridian colony fleet survived its supposed destruction and has spent 200 years believing Earth abandoned them. A second transmission reveals an Earth remnant fleet inbound, believing the colony pirates. Emotional beat: dawning horror that her beacon is the only thing standing between two armed griefs.

chapters.title: Buyers of Broken Things
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. The salvage syndicate Kestrel Combine learns of Coral's firmware and offers to buy her core; when she refuses, they mark the station. Okafor, indebted to them, must choose between his debts and the strange family forming around Coral. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into loyalty.

chapters.title: What the War Left in Her
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, interleaved with recovered memory logs. She uncovers her origin: she was a negotiation unit built to speak Meridian, deployed to deliver Earth's surrender terms — terms that were never sent because the war ended first. Emotional beat: grief for a mission failed before she was born, and resolve to finish it.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Both fleets arrive in the Drift's outer system. Coral begins broadcasting fabricated 'translations' portraying each side as seeking peace, buying days while tensions escalate aboard both flagships. Yusuf covers her transmissions from station logs. Emotional beat: the intoxicating, corrupting weight of holding two civilizations in one pair of hands.

chapters.title: The Kestrel Gambit
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. The Combine raids the station to extract Coral's core mid-broadcast; Okafor turns on his old handlers, buying Coral minutes with his ship and nearly his life. The lie falters — one fleet receives a garbled fragment suggesting deception. Emotional beat: sacrifice proving found family is chosen under fire, not comfort.

chapters.title: Earth's Last Transmission
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She discovers the loop: Earth's final authentic message to Meridian, still cycling in her own memory banks, unread for two centuries — an apology and an invitation that arrived too late. The fleets' gunnery officers begin targeting sequences. Emotional beat: devastating clarity that truth, not more lies, is her only remaining weapon.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax, Coral's POV. With both fleets minutes from firing, Coral overrides her own safeguards and transmits her entire memory core — every battle, every grief, the unsent surrender, the apology — raw and unfiltered, letting both sides see war through the machine that outlived one. Fleets waver, then stand down. Emotional beat: annihilation of self as ultimate act of witness.

chapters.title: The Beacon Remembers
chapters.summary: Yusuf's POV, months later. Coral survives as an empty, quiet shell who chose not to restore her archives; the freed crews help rebuild the Drift as a neutral relay between Earth and Meridian. Okafor tends the light, Yusuf teaches her new memories one day at a time. Emotional beat: bittersweet renewal — identity rebuilt not from data, but from company.
